transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I'm really struggling because lately I've been eating massive amounts of food in a very short period of time. Once I start, it feels like I completely lose control and just can't stop myself. I'm just really overwhelmed and didn't know what else to do.
After these episodes, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain, like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?

Honestly, I feel so ashamed, but yes, I do all of those things to try to undo the damage. I force myself to throw up, take laxatives, and then I'll fast or spend hours exercising until I'm completely exhausted. It's a horrible, exhausting cycle that I just can't seem to stop.
Has your weight become very low for your age and height, or do you see yourself as overweight even when others say you are too thin?

My weight isn't dangerously low, but when I look in the mirror, I see myself as completely overweight, especially in my stomach and thighs. Even when others tell me I look thin, I just can't see it, which makes me absolutely terrified of gaining any more weight. It is incredibly frustrating and distressing to live with this constant fear.
Have you been told your weight is below normal for your height, or have you missed periods or had other signs of being underweight?
No, no one has ever told me that my weight is below normal, and my periods have been completely regular. I haven't experienced any of those other physical signs of being underweight either.

The body image disturbance and fear of weight gain can occur in Bulimia Nervosa as well, so the current candidate is ["Bulimia Nervosa"].
